title: A negative coefficient for every n >= 8 in the Alexandersson-Kebede cycle-restricted signed sum: a refutation of Conjecture 5.2.1 (Australas. J. Combin. 86(3) (2023))
beyond_target: accepted after the campaign target of 40 was reached (additional result #46 toward 60)
exact_endpoint: AK350721.conjecture_refuted : ¬ AK350721.VoRConj ∧ ¬ AK350721.MathDBConj, where VoRConj := for all n k with 2 <= k <= n, (-1)^(n-1) * sum over pi in Perm (Fin n) with every part of pi.partition at least k of (-1)^invCount(pi) * x_rlmv(pi) * y_excv(pi) lies in the image of MvPolynomial.map (Nat.castRingHom Z), and MathDBConj is the same without the sign factor for 1 <= k <= n; both witnessed at (n,k) = (9,3) by the coefficient -1 of x_{1,5,7,8} y_{2,3,4,6,9}
scope: Conjecture 5.2.1 fails at k = 3 for every n >= 8 (ordinary proof; Lean certifies n = 9 for both the version-of-record and the MathDB/arXiv v3 wording); it holds for all 2 <= k <= n when n <= 7 (computation)

substantive_reason: It refutes a refereed conjecture on the positivity of a multivariate signed cycle-restricted permutation sum at its first new case k = 3, beyond the authors' k = 2 theorem, by an explicit monomial whose coefficient is -1 for every n >= 8, with a complete hand proof (forced prefix, eight-permutation fibre, cycle-sign cancellation) and a kernel-checked n = 9 instance that also refutes the MathDB wording non-degenerately. The failure is not a source-formula evaluation (the source has no k >= 3 data) and not a modification of a printed example.
